- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.20) or shows strong divergence (e.g., -0.02), model tends to underestimate; add 1–1.5% to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.35), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day window as baseline for smoothing.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history + negative sentiment, model often fails to reverse; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract mean reversion lag.
